governing_statute.value: Ralph C. Dills Act, Cal. Gov. Code ss. 3512-3524 (state employees)
governing_statute.quote: It is the purpose of this chapter to promote full communication between the state and its employees by providing a reasonable method of resolving disputes regarding wages, hours, and other terms and conditions of employment between the state and public employee organizations.

scope_of_bargaining.value: Wages, hours, and other terms and conditions of employment, not the merits, necessity or organization of a service or activity provided by law or executive order
scope_of_bargaining.quote: The scope of representation shall be limited to wages, hours, and other terms and conditions of employment, except, however, that the scope of representation shall not include consideration of the merits, necessity, or organization of any service or activity provided by law or executive order.

strike_legality.null_reason: The Dills Act sections captured neither grant nor prohibit strikes (s. 3514.5 only limits PERB's damages authority for an 'unlawful strike'); California public-employee strike law rests on case law that was not captured.

agency_fee_status.value: Not collectible from nonconsenting public employees under Janus v. AFSCME (2018). Fair-share-fee language remains in Gov. Code ss. 3513 and 3515.
agency_fee_status.quote: For these reasons, States and public-sector unions may no longer extract agency fees from nonconsenting employees.
agency_fee_status.pinpoint: Janus v. AFSCME, Council 31, 585 U.S. 878 (2018), Part VII
